text.what: Josh Jensen went looking for limestone in California because Burgundy grows on it, found a lime kiln site high on Mount Harlan in San Benito County, and planted pinot noir at 2,200 feet in 1975.
text.story: Jensen worked harvests at the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and at Dujac, came home with an idea about soil, and spent a year with geological survey maps before buying. Marq de Villiers wrote a book about the place in 1993.

kin.as: Who chose the limestone and planted it.
The cuttings that came home with him, and what growers now call them.
The comparison he was explicitly chasing.
